title: Nahum
paragraphs: A prophecy concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite. God is jealous, and the LORD (Yahweh) takes vengeance. The LORD takes vengeance and is filled with wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his enemies and holds his anger against his foes. The LORD is slow to anger but immense in power; he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust beneath his feet. He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossoms of Lebanon fade. The mountains quake before him and the hills dissolve. The earth trembles at his presence — the world and all who live in it.

Who can withstand his fury? Who can endure the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire; the rocks shatter before him. The LORD is good — a refuge in times of trouble. He cares for those who trust in him. But with an overwhelming flood he will bring Nineveh to an end; he will pursue his enemies into darkness. Whatever you plot against the LORD, he will bring to a complete end. Trouble will not rise a second time. Though they are tangled like thorns and soaked like drunkards, they will be consumed like dry stubble.

One has come from you who plots evil against the LORD — a wicked counselor. This is what the LORD says: Though they are at full strength and many in number, they will still be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, Judah, I will afflict you no more. Now I will break his yoke from your neck and snap your chains. The LORD has issued a decree about you, Nineveh: You will have no descendants to carry on your name. I will destroy the carved images and cast idols in your gods' temple. I will prepare your grave, for you are vile. Look! On the mountains, the feet of the one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your festivals, Judah, and fulfill your vows, for the wicked will never invade you again — they are completely destroyed.

The attacker advances against you, Nineveh. Guard the fortress, watch the road, brace yourselves, summon all your strength! For the LORD is restoring the majesty of Jacob, like the majesty of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and ruined their vines. The shields of his warriors are red; the soldiers are dressed in scarlet. The metal on the chariots flashes like fire on the day they are made ready; the cypress spears are brandished. The chariots race madly through the streets, rushing back and forth through the squares. They look like flaming torches, darting like lightning.

The river gates are thrown open and the palace collapses. It is decreed: the city is stripped bare, carried away. Her slave girls moan like doves, beating their breasts. Nineveh is like a leaking pool — its people are draining away. "Stop! Stop!" they cry, but no one turns back. Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure — a wealth of every kind of precious thing. She is pillaged, plundered, stripped! Hearts melt, knees buckle, every body trembles, every face turns pale.

Where now is the lions' den, the place where they fed their young, where the lion and lioness went and the cubs had nothing to fear? The lion tore enough prey for his cubs and strangled prey for his mates, filling his lair with the kill and his dens with torn flesh. "I am against you," declares the LORD of Hosts. "I will burn your chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voices of your messengers will no longer be heard."

Doom to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without victims! The crack of whips, the clatter of wheels, galloping horses and jolting chariots! Charging cavalry, flashing swords and glittering spears! Masses of casualties, heaps of the dead, bodies without end — people stumble over the corpses. All because of the wanton lust of the seductive prostitute, the mistress of sorceries, who enslaved nations by her prostitution and peoples by her witchcraft. "I am against you," declares the LORD of Hosts. "I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame."

"I will pelt you with filth. I will treat you with contempt and make you a spectacle. Everyone who sees you will flee from you and say, 'Nineveh is in ruins — who will mourn for her?' Where can I find anyone to comfort you?" Are you better than Thebes, situated along the Nile, with water all around her — the river her defense, the waters her wall? Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies. Yet she was carried into exile; she went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at every street corner. Lots were cast for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.

You too will stagger like a drunkard; you will go into hiding, seeking refuge from the enemy. All your fortresses are like fig trees with ripe fruit — when shaken, the figs fall straight into the mouth of the eater. Look at your troops — they are all weaklings. The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has consumed your defenses. Draw water for the siege! Strengthen your fortifications! Work the clay, tread the mortar, repair the brick mold! Yet fire will consume you there; the sword will cut you down and devour you like a swarm of locusts. Multiply like grasshoppers, multiply like locusts!

You have increased the number of your merchants until they outnumber the stars. But like locusts, they strip the land and then fly away. Your officials are like swarms of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day — but when the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where. Your shepherds are asleep, king of Assyria; your nobles slumber in the dust. Your people are scattered across the mountains with no one to gather them. There is no healing for your wound; your injury is fatal. Everyone who hears the news about you claps their hands at your fall, for who has not suffered from your endless cruelty?
